question: The Mozilla Firefox/Google Chrome/Microsoft Edge requires support for the __________ protocol.
solution:
The correct answer is __HTTP 1.1**(Hypertext Transfer Protocol)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• HTTP__ stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
 
• HTTP 1.1 is a version of the HTTP protocol used for communication between web browsers and servers.
 
• This protocol allows the transfer of hypertext documents and other resources.
 
• It supports persistent connections, meaning multiple requests and responses can be exchanged over a single connection.
 
• HTTP 1.1 introduced improvements over HTTP 1.0, such as chunked transfer encoding and caching mechanisms.
 
• It is widely supported by modern web browsers, including Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome, and Microsoft Edge.
 
• Enhanced performance and reduced latency were key advancements in HTTP 1.1.
 
• The protocol is essential for delivering websites and web applications efficiently.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **HTTP 2:**

 
 
• HTTP/2 is a newer version of the HTTP protocol designed to improve web performance.
 
• It supports multiplexing, header compression, and server push.
 
 
 
• **HTTP 3:**
 
 
• HTTP/3 is based on the QUIC protocol, offering faster and more reliable connections.
 
• It eliminates head-of-line blocking issues found in HTTP/2.
 
 
 
• **HTTPS:**
 
 
• HTTPS is a secure version of HTTP, ensuring encrypted communication.
 
• It uses SSL/TLS protocols for security.
